prerequisites: Basic knowledge of physics and electronics
Mathematics skills (especially vector and matrix calculus)

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the concepts and many system-technical solutions for imaging sensor technology.
They also know elementary image processing algorithms to extract knowledge from images.
Students are able to develop technological solutions with imaging sensor technologies for practice-oriented problems and to specify the technological steps for their realization.
Students have practical experience in problem-oriented conception and application of imaging sensor systems.
They can also appropriately apply and combine image processing algorithms.

Students can independently conceive and realize problem-oriented system solutions based on imaging sensor techniques and image processing algorithms. Imaging sensor technologies/Imaging is to be understood as a system technology that has strong connections to electronics, computer science, sensor technology and human vision; system thinking is therefore strongly anchored in the subject.

syllabus_topics: Imaging camera systems (Examples: Spectral Imaging, high-speed cameras, light-shadow sensors, 3D-Imaging)
Image processing (point operations, filters, object extraction)
assessment_rules: The graded assessment can be a project report (approx. 15-20 pages with an approx. 20-minute explanation), an oral examination, or a written examination (Klausur), as determined by the examination regulations. An ungraded experimental work, potentially as an 'Advanced Internship' with approximately 5 experiments, is also required. The choice of graded assessment method is not explicitly weighted.
